Write ONE factual paragraph of 30–200 words explaining the recorded comparison for Jennifer Brouhard. The guide's issue focus is Palestinian justice, including Gaza, arms transfers, divestment, civil liberties, and relevant recommendations. Consider all supplied observations and preserve substantive contrary evidence. Describe concrete statements, votes, sponsorships, pledges, and exact recommendation tiers; do not rescore or choose a different candidate. N/A means unassessed, not favorable or unfavorable. Relevant N/A observations remain context. An absent entry does not establish that a candidate has never said or done something. State a refusal, opposition or shortfall only when explicitly supported, not from a missing record. Do not fault state or local officeholders for not exercising congressional powers. Use only issue-relevant facts; omit unrelated platform lists, missing-record disclaimers, source-upload mechanics, grading methodology and generic uncertainty padding. When an actual statement date is unknown, omit the date; never substitute upload metadata. Preserve Preferred, Ally, supported, opposed and endorsed as distinct source terms. Mention endorsement organizations only from the two explicit relevant-record lists above; omit other backing even when it appears elsewhere in the source state. Describe super-PAC money as independent spending supporting or opposing the candidate, not campaign contributions. Use current structured spending amounts when giving current totals; do not substitute an older narrative total. Avoid overclaiming a bill's provisions from its name. Do not use rubric descriptions as independent factual evidence. No numeric score, grade, confidence, threshold, voting instruction, demographic appeal, outside knowledge or invented fact. Name the office once. Plain prose, no lists or headings. Output ONLY the paragraph.

Samir Laymoun source policy: omit his support, opposition and comments from voter prose when other relevant directional evidence exists. Do not retain his opinion anonymously as 'an activist' or 'a personal guide'. Exceptions: the Kamal Yassin race, or a candidate for whom his opinion is the only relevant directional evidence. Check the complete current research, not just an old summary. Where allowed, state the support/opposition or relevant comment briefly and accurately. Never relabel his opinion as BAMC Action's position or as the candidate's own policy. Never explain that he is an individual rather than an institution, an activist opinion source, owner-requested, or separate from official organizational positions. Those classifications belong in the audit, not the voter paragraph. Preserve genuinely material facts and qualifications; do not turn a tactical recommendation into agreement on policy.
LEGISLATIVE CONSISTENCY: Each legislative action has a date/period, response, and tracker alignment. Keep these together. Aligned means aligned with the tracker, not a negative item. A No vote against defunding universities for boycotting Israel is aligned when the record says aligned; never describe it as cutting the other way. A Yes vote can support an adverse bill. Not voting, Not elected, neutral and unknown are not contrary votes. Distinguish sponsorship, a pledge to sponsor, and a recorded vote. Do not merge differently dated bills or turn a period into an exact vote date. Use the structured evidence, not an earlier narrative, to resolve meaning. Write a factual comparison of the supplied observations and saved selection, without voting instructions or identity-based appeals.

Write factual, descriptive research prose without appeals to a demographic audience, identity-based appeals or voting instructions. Explain the documented observations and saved assessment. Preserve substantive contrary evidence and state versus federal powers. Never treat an upload date as a statement date; when the statement date is unknown, omit the date from prose rather than explaining upload metadata. Do not list unrelated platform topics or say the platform is silent on the issue. Distinguish a stated intention from an actual action. Keep recommendation tiers exact: Ally, supported and Preferred are not automatically formal endorsements. No missing-record disclaimer padding. A recorded aligned No vote must never be called contrary or negative. Consider every supplied observation; cover all of them when an evidence audit is requested. Prose must accurately reflect the resulting record. Rubric descriptions are not independent factual evidence about bill text or candidate actions; do not turn them into facts absent from the supplied candidate record.
